Subject: Aligning annual prepay + drawdown telemetry

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. For our ACME HealthTech rollout we need a clear invoicing cadence for the annual committed spend and a simple way to track drawdowns across the year (ideally a weekly/biweekly snapshot). Procurement asked for:

- An invoice template they can pre-approve for PO/Net30 flow
- A drawdown "heatmap" they can import into their ledger team (CSV ok)
- A recommended cadence (monthly or quarterly invoices) and how Redwood will surface actual vs committed usage to us

Can you share a sample invoice + a short ops runbook so we can loop procurement and accounting? We have a tentative PO but need the invoice pattern to attach.

Appreciate it — Sarah

--
Sarah Miles

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning annual prepay + drawdown telemetry

Hi Sarah —

Thanks, this is straightforward. High-level proposal below and I attached a sample invoice and a drawdown heatmap CSV that our accounting ops uses. Quick call available tomorrow if you want to walk through live.

Proposed invoicing cadence (recommendation):
- Quarterly invoices billed against the annual prepay commitment. Quarterly keeps GL clean for customers on Net30 but still aligns to usage windows. We can do monthly if ACME prefers finer granularity.

Drawdown telemetry:
- We’ll deliver a weekly CSV export: columns = week_start, week_end, committed_balance_start, committed_balance_end, tokens_drawn, effective_rate, notes. The attached heatmap is a sample export that maps tranches to calendar weeks.

Other operational notes:
- Invoice numbering: Redwood uses RWD-YYYY-####. We can include your PO number in the invoice reference.
- Tax/VAT: For US entities, invoices are net of VAT. If ACME needs EU VAT routing we’ll add the VAT section and local remit instructions.
- Contract alignment: we’ll mirror the committed spend breakouts in the invoice line items so your ledger can match without manual mapping.

Attachments included: invoice-sample-redwood-annual-prepay.pdf (PDF), drawdown-conductor-heatmap.csv (CSV).

If that looks good I’ll loop Kim on final numbering and have accounting prepare the first quarterly invoice.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 206 555 0123
[Attachments: invoice-sample-redwood-annual-prepay.pdf (PDF, stub), drawdown-conductor-heatmap.csv (CSV, stub)]

Agree with Laura. A couple of operational clarifications from my side:
- Billing run date: suggest we set the billing run on the 3rd business day after quarter close (gives usage reconciliation time).
- Drawdown alerts: we can push weekly usage deltas to a shared S3/drive and create threshold alerts (e.g., 15% and 5% remaining). Would you like those pushed to your accounting mailbox or to a shared SFTP?
- PO mapping: we’ll add a "Customer PO" field to the invoice PDF and the CSV header so matching is one-to-one.

If Brightlane confirms weekly CSV -> SFTP, Kim can schedule the first automated export and we can tag the HubSpot deal with the invoice cadence.

— Jonas
Senior Manager, Billing Integrations | Redwood Inference
